title: Packaged smoke can validate and shut down the wrong instance
test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js (23 new tests): 'with a server already answering on the smoke port, the smoke exits before launching and sends it nothing' (runs the real script against a fake Nextra on 31847), 'a child that exits before readiness stops the stages at once, with its exit code', 'a spawn error stops the stages at once', 'a child exit during the static shell, handshake or package-info stage stops the run at once', 'a ready server that is not the launched executable or its descendant fails readiness before any stage', 'kill-media-worker is sent only while the PID serving the port is owned by the run', 'recovery adopts the replacement the original server starts as its child, while the launched child keeps running', 'a same-build copy that does not descend from the still-running launched child is not adopted', 'a code-0 exit of the child after kill-media-worker is accepted is a handover: recovery passes once the replacement is adopted', 'a late code-0 child exit after the replacement was adopted is still tolerated', 'without an adopted replacement the recovery stage fails at its deadline and reports the child exit', 'a non-zero or signalled child exit during recovery fails it at once', 'a replacement that does not run from the launched build is not adopted, and recovery fails', 'a simulated packaged run passes every stage in order, each destructive request right after an ownership check', 'the cleanup shutdown request goes only to a server the run owns', 'the pre-launch probe refuses a port where anything answers, and passes only a refused connection', plus unit tests for classifyChildExit, createChildExitMonitor, setPhase ordering, the process-list parsers (ppid), isDescendant, caxaApplicationDirectory and decideReplacementAdoption
proof: Holds. The smoke used the fixed endpoint 127.0.0.1:31847 without checking who served it, only logged a child 'error' and never watched the child's exit. Before the fix the new tests failed 23 of 23 on the unchanged script (the 11 TASK-050 tests still passed). The decisive one runs node scripts/smoke-packaged.js with a launchable executable (a copy of node.exe under a unique temp path, which exits at once) while a fake ready Nextra holds port 31847. The unchanged smoke printed 'Starting packaged executable on port 31847...' and 'Initial packaged readiness passed.', ignored the child's immediate exit, and sent the foreign instance GET /readyz, GET /, GET /socket.io/, GET /api/package-info, GET /api/metrics and then POST /api/test/kill-media-worker. It was still polling that instance when the test killed it after 15 s. (With a non-executable file, Windows' spawn threw EFTYPE synchronously, so the first attempt did not reach the stages; the test uses a real executable for that reason.) The other 22 failed because the helpers did not exist ('smoke.createChildExitMonitor is not a function'). Fix, in scripts/smoke-packaged.js only. assertSmokePortFree probes /healthz before the baseline and the spawn: any answer throws 'Smoke port 31847 is occupied: ... answered HTTP <status>', a timeout or other error throws 'is not free', and only ECONNREFUSED goes on. classifyChildExit({ phase, code, signal, error }) follows the prompt's table. createChildExitMonitor(child) records { code, signal, phase, at }; setPhase moves forward only, over starting/stages/recovery/post-recovery/shutdown/cleanup; exited never rejects and also settles on a spawn failure; unexpected rejects only for an unexpected exit or any 'error', and carries an internal no-op catch. createRunContext holds the child, the monitor, ownedPids (seeded with child.pid), servingPid, ownership { caxaDirectory, portObservedUnowned } and an AbortSignal that the stages' fetches and sleeps use. An unexpected exit aborts that signal, so a failed stage leaves no polling behind. Every stage up to the media-worker replacement runs through raceUnexpected. After readiness, verifyLaunchedServer requires the /api/metrics process.pid to be the child or a descendant of it (listProcesses now returns ppid: Win32_Process ParentProcessId, ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,args=) and records its caxa extraction (nextra-<id>/<attempt>). checkMediaWorkerReplacement refuses kill-media-worker unless the metrics PID is owned, and enters 'recovery' right before the POST. It adopts a new PID under the Q-002 default (the port was never answered by an unowned process, and the PID runs from the same caxa extraction). One tightening on top: while the launched child is still running, the PID must also descend from it. Since TASK-058 the server starts the replacement as a child of the original process, so this holds for the real replacement, and it rejects another instance of the same build, which shares the extraction. Only after the child has exited (a handover) is ancestry not required. Any other answer fails the stage at once. The stage passes only with an adopted PID, readiness and a new worker PID, then enters 'post-recovery'; at the deadline it fails and names the recorded child exit. checkGracefulShutdown and cleanup's best-effort shutdown POST go only to an owned PID (cleanup also accepts a descendant of the child). After the fix: the smoke test file passes 34 of 34. The port test exits 1 in about 0.1 s with 'Smoke port 31847 is occupied' and no launch line, and the foreign instance received only GET /healthz. By hand (not committed), node scripts/smoke-packaged.js with a copied node.exe as the executable exited 1 after 4.3 s, most of it PowerShell process listings, with 'Packaged executable (PID 32504) exited unexpectedly in phase 'starting' (code 0, no signal).' instead of the 30 s readiness wait. Not run: the approval-gated packaged smoke on Windows and macOS (no packaged executable was built in this lane, and the prompt says to ask first). The real stub's behaviour during recovery (Q-EXIT-001) is therefore not observed yet. The harness now logs it: 'Launched executable during recovery: still running.' or 'exited (code, signal) in phase ...', and a 'Launched executable (PID n) exited ...' line on every exit.
